text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ivan Prskalo, Croat mayor of Mostar, denies European Union administrator Sir Martin Garrod's claim that there is no security in Croat-controlled west Mostar and that mafia runs town. Deputy mayor Safet Orucevic, a Moslem, insists mafia or others engage in acts that damage all citizens of Mostar.
- Sejfudin Tokic says his Bosnian opposition Joint List won't take part in municipal elections in November if manipulation of voting lists not solved.

- "Presidency building in Sarajevo is completely secure because it is well guarded, so officials have conditions for normal work," says Sejdalija Mustafic, general secretary of presidency replying to claims of new elected Serb member of the presidency, Momcilo Krajisnik, that he will not be safe there. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
